questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: Which of the following actions most clearly creates an express agency relationship between a seller and a real estate broker?

answers.text: The seller and broker discussing potential listing prices over coffee
The seller giving the broker permission to walk through the property
The seller and broker signing a written listing agreement
The broker placing a sign on the property without the seller's knowledge

explanations.a: Casual discussion of price does not grant authority to represent and falls short of forming an express agency.
explanations.b: Permission to enter the property is mere access, not a grant of authority to act on the seller's behalf.
explanations.c: A signed listing agreement is the classic written, express grant of authority that creates an express agency relationship.
explanations.d: An agent cannot create authority unilaterally; only the principal can grant authority to represent.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A buyer asks a licensee questions about a property and follows the licensee's advice on negotiating an offer, although no written agreement exists. The relationship that may have been formed is BEST described as which of the following?

answers.text: express agency
implied agency
designated agency
universal agency

explanations.a: Express agency requires a clear oral or written agreement to represent, which the facts here do not show.
explanations.b: Implied agency arises from the parties' conduct rather than an express agreement and is the relationship suggested by these facts.
explanations.c: Designated agency requires a brokerage to formally assign different licensees to each party in a transaction.
explanations.d: Universal agency grants broad authority over a principal's affairs and does not arise from a single negotiation.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: In a transaction in which one brokerage firm represents both the buyer and the seller through its licensees, the agency relationship that exists is MOST accurately classified as which of the following?

answers.text: single agency
subagency
customer agency
dual agency

explanations.a: Single agency means representing only one party in a transaction, which is not what is described.
explanations.b: Subagency involves a cooperating broker working on behalf of the listing broker's principal, not joint representation.
explanations.c: There is no recognized 'customer agency' relationship; a customer is a non-represented party.
explanations.d: When one firm represents both buyer and seller in the same transaction, the firm is acting as a dual agent.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A seller's agent learns that the seller will accept much less than the listed price. Which fiduciary duty PROHIBITS the agent from sharing this information with a buyer?

answers.text: confidentiality
accounting
obedience
care

explanations.a: Confidentiality prohibits disclosing information that could weaken the principal's bargaining position, including a willingness to accept less than the list price.
explanations.b: The duty of accounting concerns the proper handling and reporting of money and property, not the disclosure of negotiating positions.
explanations.c: Obedience requires following the principal's lawful instructions but is not what bars sharing confidential price information.
explanations.d: The duty of care concerns acting with reasonable competence and skill, not the protection of confidential information.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: Although a buyer's agent owes loyalty to the buyer, the agent must still treat the seller honestly. The duty owed to the seller in this case is BEST described as which of the following?

answers.text: loyalty
diligence
honesty and fair dealing
reasonable skill and care

explanations.a: Loyalty is owed only to a client, not to the other side of the transaction.
explanations.b: Diligence is a duty owed to the client to pursue their interests vigorously, not a duty owed to the opposing party.
explanations.c: Agents owe non-client parties the duty of honesty and fair dealing, including avoiding misrepresentation.
explanations.d: Reasonable skill and care is owed to the client when carrying out the agency; it is not the duty owed to a non-client.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A listing agreement can terminate by all of the following events EXCEPT:

answers.text: destruction of the listed property
the listing salesperson moving to a different brokerage firm
the death of the seller
mutual agreement of seller and broker

explanations.a: Destruction of the subject matter terminates the agency by impossibility of performance.
explanations.b: The listing belongs to the brokerage firm, not the individual salesperson, so the salesperson's move does not terminate it.
explanations.c: Death of the principal terminates an agency relationship by operation of law.
explanations.d: Parties may always agree to rescind a contract by mutual consent.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A real estate licensee who is acting as the seller's agent must disclose that representation to a prospective buyer at which of the following times?

answers.text: at the first substantive contact with the buyer
only at the closing of the transaction
only if the buyer specifically asks about representation
after an offer has been accepted

explanations.a: Agency disclosure laws generally require the licensee to reveal representation at the first substantive contact so the buyer is not misled about whose interests are being protected.
explanations.b: Waiting until closing defeats the purpose of disclosure, which is to inform the buyer before substantive negotiation.
explanations.c: Disclosure is mandatory and does not depend on the buyer asking about it.
explanations.d: Disclosure after acceptance is far too late; the buyer needs the information to make decisions during negotiation.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A licensee learns from the seller that the basement has flooded twice in the past year. When showing the property to buyers, the licensee should:

answers.text: mention it only if a buyer specifically asks about water damage
refuse to show the property until the seller fixes the issue
share the information only with buyers who appear serious
disclose the material fact to all prospective buyers

explanations.a: Material facts about the condition of the property must be disclosed even if the buyer does not specifically ask.
explanations.b: A licensee has no authority to refuse to show a properly listed property based on a defect.
explanations.c: Disclosure cannot be selectively withheld from less-serious buyers; the duty applies to all prospective purchasers.
explanations.d: Repeated flooding is a material defect, and the licensee's duty of honest dealing requires disclosure to all prospective buyers.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A listing agreement in which the seller promises to pay a commission to the broker, and the broker promises to use diligence in finding a buyer, is which type of contract?

answers.text: unilateral
unenforceable
bilateral
implied

explanations.a: A unilateral contract involves a promise made in exchange for an act, not a mutual exchange of promises.
explanations.b: An unenforceable contract is one a court will not enforce despite being otherwise formed, which is not what this exchange of promises describes.
explanations.c: When both parties exchange promises, the contract is bilateral.
explanations.d: An implied contract arises from conduct rather than an explicit exchange of promises.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: For a real estate sales contract to be valid, all of the following are required EXCEPT:

answers.text: legally competent parties
an earnest money deposit from the buyer
an offer and acceptance
consideration

explanations.a: Competent parties are an essential element; without capacity the contract is not enforceable.
explanations.b: Earnest money is customary and demonstrates good faith but is not a required element of contract validity.
explanations.c: Mutual assent expressed through offer and acceptance is required to form any contract.
explanations.d: Consideration, the bargained-for exchange of value, is essential to contract validity.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A 16-year-old signs a contract to purchase a house. The contract is BEST described as which of the following?

answers.text: voidable at the option of the minor
void from inception
fully enforceable against both parties
valid only if notarized

explanations.a: Contracts entered into by minors are voidable at the minor's option, which protects them from being bound by improvident bargains.
explanations.b: A minor's contract is not automatically void from the start; it is enforceable until the minor disaffirms.
explanations.c: The adult counterparty may be bound, but the minor cannot be forced to perform.
explanations.d: Notarization does not transform an otherwise voidable contract by a minor into a fully binding one.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A buyer signs an offer and the listing agent emails the seller's signed acceptance to the buyer's agent at 8:00 p.m. The acceptance is generally considered communicated to the buyer when:

answers.text: the buyer reads the email the next morning
the buyer's agent receives the emailed acceptance
the seller signs the document
the broker forwards the document to closing

explanations.a: Notice generally takes effect on receipt, not when the principal personally reads the message.
explanations.b: Notice to the agent is treated as notice to the principal, so receipt by the buyer's agent communicates the acceptance to the buyer.
explanations.c: Signing alone, without communication, does not complete contract formation.
explanations.d: Forwarding the executed document to closing happens after the contract is already formed.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A real estate sales contract has been signed by both parties but the closing has not yet occurred. The contract is BEST described as which of the following?

answers.text: void
rescinded
executed
executory

explanations.a: A void contract has no legal force; this contract is binding and waiting to be performed.
explanations.b: Rescission ends a contract by mutual agreement or court order, which is not what is described.
explanations.c: An executed contract is one in which both parties have fully performed, which has not yet occurred here.
explanations.d: A contract that is binding but not yet fully performed is executory.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: An oral agreement to sell a parcel of land for $250,000 is generally:

answers.text: fully enforceable so long as witnesses are present
enforceable only if a deposit is paid
unenforceable under the Statute of Frauds
valid only between family members

explanations.a: Witnesses do not satisfy the writing requirement; the Statute of Frauds calls for a writing signed by the party to be charged.
explanations.b: A deposit alone does not cure the lack of a written agreement, although partial performance may sometimes substitute in equity.
explanations.c: Contracts for the sale of an interest in real property must generally be in writing to be enforceable under the Statute of Frauds.
explanations.d: Family relationships have no bearing on the Statute of Frauds, which applies to all real estate contracts.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: In a typical purchase contract, the party who promises to convey the property is referred to as the:

answers.text: grantor
devisee
lessee
mortgagee

explanations.a: The grantor is the party conveying title or a property interest to another.
explanations.b: A devisee receives real property under a will, not under a contract for sale.
explanations.c: A lessee is a tenant who holds a leasehold interest, not a party conveying ownership.
explanations.d: A mortgagee is a lender holding a security interest, not the party conveying the property.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: Earnest money provided by a buyer with an offer to purchase serves PRIMARILY to:

answers.text: cover the seller's legal fees
pay the listing broker's commission
transfer ownership of the property
demonstrate the buyer's good-faith intent to perform

explanations.a: The seller's legal fees are normally paid from the seller's own funds, not from buyer's earnest money.
explanations.b: Commission is paid at closing from the seller's proceeds, not directly from the earnest money.
explanations.c: Ownership transfers by deed at closing, not by depositing earnest money.
explanations.d: Earnest money primarily evidences the buyer's serious, good-faith commitment to perform the contract.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.keyword: option holder's right but not obligation
questions.text: An option contract gives the option holder which of the following rights?

answers.text: immediate ownership of the property at signing
the right, but not the obligation, to purchase the property within a stated period
the obligation to purchase the property at a future closing
an automatic right of first refusal on neighboring parcels

explanations.a: Title does not pass when an option is granted; it transfers only if the option is later exercised and the sale closes.
explanations.b: An option grants the holder a unilateral right to buy within the option period, with no duty to do so.
explanations.c: An option imposes no obligation to buy; if it did, it would be a binding sales contract.
explanations.d: Right of first refusal is a separate concept that does not automatically attach to neighboring property.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.keyword: time is of the essence clause
questions.text: A purchase contract clause stating that 'time is of the essence' generally means which of the following?

answers.text: the closing date can be extended without penalty
either party may withdraw at any reasonable time
specified deadlines must be met or a party may be in default
the seller controls the timing of all contingencies

explanations.a: Time-is-of-the-essence language tightens deadlines rather than allowing free extensions.
explanations.b: The clause does not give either party an arbitrary right to withdraw.
explanations.c: When time is of the essence, missing a contractual deadline can constitute a material breach.
explanations.d: The clause applies equally to both parties; it does not give the seller unilateral control over timing.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A buyer fails to close on the agreed date despite being able to do so, and the seller has properly tendered performance. The seller's remedies typically include all of the following EXCEPT:

answers.text: forcing the buyer to accept ownership of a different property
retaining the buyer's earnest money as liquidated damages, if the contract so provides
suing for specific performance
suing for monetary damages

explanations.a: A seller cannot substitute a different property; remedies must arise from the original contract.
explanations.b: If the contract treats earnest money as liquidated damages, the seller may keep it on a buyer's default.
explanations.c: Specific performance is available where money damages are inadequate, including in real estate.
explanations.d: Monetary damages for the loss caused by the buyer's breach are a standard contract remedy.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A seller responds to a buyer's offer by changing the closing date and increasing the price. The seller's response is BEST described as which of the following?

answers.text: an unconditional acceptance
a counteroffer that rejects the original offer
a contingent acceptance that keeps the original offer open
an option agreement

explanations.a: Changing material terms is not unconditional acceptance.
explanations.b: Modifying material terms operates as a rejection of the original offer and creates a new counteroffer.
explanations.c: Once a counteroffer is made, the original offer is extinguished and cannot remain open.
explanations.d: An option agreement requires consideration and a defined option period; that is not what occurred here.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A buyer submits a written offer that states it must be accepted within 48 hours. Twelve hours later, before the seller has responded, the buyer notifies the seller in writing that the offer is withdrawn. The offer is:

answers.text: binding on the buyer until the 48 hours expires
binding only if the seller has already begun to act on it
effectively revoked because acceptance had not yet been communicated
void only if the seller has not seen it

explanations.a: An ordinary offer with a stated time limit may still be revoked at any point before acceptance unless supported by separate consideration.
explanations.b: Reliance is not the standard for revocability of an ordinary offer; communication of revocation before acceptance ends it.
explanations.c: Without consideration making the offer irrevocable, the buyer may revoke at any time before the seller communicates acceptance.
explanations.d: Whether the seller has seen the offer is irrelevant; what matters is whether acceptance has been communicated.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A purchase contract is contingent on the buyer obtaining financing within 30 days. If the buyer makes a good-faith effort but is unable to secure financing in that period, the buyer is generally entitled to:

answers.text: reduce the purchase price by the loan amount
extend the closing indefinitely without seller consent
demand that the seller provide owner financing
terminate the contract and recover the earnest money

explanations.a: Contingency failure does not entitle the buyer to a unilateral price reduction.
explanations.b: Extensions require the seller's agreement; a contingency failure does not grant unlimited time.
explanations.c: The seller has no obligation to provide owner financing simply because the buyer's financing fell through.
explanations.d: When a financing contingency cannot be satisfied despite a good-faith effort, the buyer is typically entitled to terminate and recover the earnest money.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.objective: 1C8 Duties and obligations of the parties
questions.keyword: seller's obligation to deliver marketable title
questions.text: Under most purchase contracts, the seller's primary obligation at closing is to:

answers.text: deliver marketable title in the manner specified by the contract
provide a home warranty for one year
arrange and pay for the buyer's financing
pay all of the buyer's closing costs

explanations.a: Conveying marketable title in the form required by the contract is the seller's central duty at closing.
explanations.b: Home warranties are negotiable items, not a default seller obligation.
explanations.c: Financing is the buyer's responsibility unless the contract specifically provides otherwise.
explanations.d: Closing costs are allocated by contract; the seller is not automatically responsible for the buyer's costs.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A listing agreement is a contract between which of the following parties?

answers.text: the buyer and the seller
the seller and the listing broker
the listing broker and the cooperating broker
the seller and a prospective buyer

explanations.a: A buyer-seller contract is the purchase agreement, not a listing.
explanations.b: A listing agreement is between the seller, as principal, and the listing broker, as agent.
explanations.c: An agreement between brokers is a cooperating-broker or referral arrangement, not a listing.
explanations.d: A seller and a prospective buyer enter into a purchase contract, not a listing agreement.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: All of the following are typical provisions of a written listing agreement EXCEPT:

answers.text: the listing price
the duration of the listing
the compensation to be paid
the buyer's source of financing

explanations.a: The listing price is a core term that the listing agreement must specify.
explanations.b: A definite duration is required so the parties know when the listing ends.
explanations.c: The amount and method of broker compensation is a fundamental listing term.
explanations.d: The buyer's financing is addressed in the purchase contract; it is not part of the listing agreement.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.keyword: broker duty to disclose material defect
questions.text: A listing broker discovers that the seller failed to disclose a known structural defect to a prospective buyer. The broker's duty requires the broker to:

answers.text: disclose the known material defect to the buyer regardless of the seller's wishes
follow the seller's instructions and remain silent
terminate the listing without explanation
disclose the defect only after a contract is signed

explanations.a: A broker's duty of honesty to non-clients overrides a client's instruction to conceal a known material defect.
explanations.b: Obedience to the principal does not extend to following unlawful or fraudulent instructions.
explanations.c: Quietly walking away does not remedy the misrepresentation that a buyer would face.
explanations.d: Waiting until after the contract is signed defeats the disclosure's purpose and may expose the broker to liability.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A seller and broker mutually agree in writing to cancel an existing listing agreement before its expiration. This termination is BEST classified as:

answers.text: abandonment by the broker
breach of contract by the seller
mutual rescission
operation of law

explanations.a: Abandonment requires unilateral disengagement by one party, not a mutual agreement.
explanations.b: Cancellation by mutual consent is not a breach; both parties have agreed to end the contract.
explanations.c: When the parties jointly agree to cancel a contract, that is mutual rescission.
explanations.d: Operation of law refers to events such as death or bankruptcy, not voluntary written agreement.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A real estate commission earned by a broker under an exclusive-right-to-sell listing is generally:

answers.text: paid only if the listing broker personally finds the buyer
owed to the broker if the property sells during the listing period, regardless of who procures the buyer
divided equally with any other broker who shows the property
owed only after closing costs are deducted from the seller's proceeds

explanations.a: Limiting payment to the listing broker's own buyer would describe an exclusive agency, not exclusive right to sell.
explanations.b: Exclusive-right-to-sell entitles the listing broker to compensation when the property sells during the listing period, no matter who procures the buyer.
explanations.c: Cooperating brokers are paid pursuant to separate offers of cooperation, not by automatic equal split.
explanations.d: Commission is determined by the listing terms and is generally calculated from the gross sales price, not from net proceeds.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: In which type of listing agreement does the seller retain the right to sell the property personally without owing a commission, while still allowing the broker to market the property?

answers.text: exclusive-right-to-sell
net listing
open listing among multiple brokers
exclusive-agency listing

explanations.a: An exclusive-right-to-sell entitles the broker to a commission even if the seller finds the buyer.
explanations.b: A net listing pays the broker any amount over a stated net to the seller and is unrelated to the seller's right to sell directly.
explanations.c: An open listing allows multiple brokers but does not specifically address whether the seller can sell directly without commission.
explanations.d: Exclusive agency gives one broker the exclusive right among brokers, while preserving the seller's right to sell personally without owing a commission.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.objective: 1E Employment agreements between broker and licensees
questions.text: A licensee who is classified as an independent contractor by a brokerage firm is generally:

answers.text: responsible for paying her own self-employment taxes
entitled to standard employee benefits from the broker
paid an hourly wage subject to overtime rules
unable to receive commission-based compensation

explanations.a: Independent contractors handle their own self-employment taxes because the broker does not withhold for them.
explanations.b: Standard employee benefits such as health insurance and paid leave are not provided to independent contractors.
explanations.c: Independent contractors are not paid hourly wages and are not subject to overtime rules.
explanations.d: Commission-based compensation is in fact one of the hallmarks of independent contractor licensee arrangements.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.keyword: duty of accounting and trust funds
questions.text: A licensee receives an earnest money check from a buyer at the time the offer is signed. The licensee's fiduciary duty of accounting requires the licensee to:

answers.text: promptly deliver the funds to the broker for deposit into the brokerage's trust account
personally hold the check uncashed until the closing date
endorse the check directly to the seller upon receipt
cash the check and store the proceeds in the licensee's personal account

explanations.a: Funds belonging to others must be promptly turned over to the broker for deposit in a designated trust or escrow account so they can be properly accounted for.
explanations.b: Holding an uncashed check sidesteps the trust account requirement and exposes the funds to loss.
explanations.c: The licensee may not unilaterally redirect the buyer's earnest money to the seller; the funds belong in trust until disbursement is authorized.
explanations.d: Commingling client funds with personal funds is a serious violation of the duty of accounting and of license law.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A listing agreement provides that it runs from January 1 through June 30. On July 1, with no further action by either party, the listing has terminated by:

answers.text: abandonment
rescission
expiration of its stated term
revocation by the broker

explanations.a: Abandonment requires the broker to walk away from duties before the term ends, which is not described here.
explanations.b: Rescission requires affirmative action by the parties to undo the agreement, not the mere passage of time.
explanations.c: When a listing reaches its stated end date with no extension, it terminates automatically by expiration of the term.
explanations.d: Revocation involves the broker affirmatively ending the agency early, not the natural end of the term.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A licensee meets a buyer at an open house who has not signed any buyer-broker agreement. With respect to the listing licensee's role, the unrepresented buyer is BEST classified as a:

answers.text: prospect
principal
client
customer

explanations.a: Prospect is a marketing term, not a defined real estate agency status.
explanations.b: A principal is the party who has engaged the agent, which the unrepresented buyer has not done.
explanations.c: A client is a represented party in an agency relationship, which this buyer is not.
explanations.d: A non-represented party to whom the licensee owes only honesty and fair dealing is properly called a customer.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A homeowner publicly offers a $1,000 reward to anyone who finds and returns her lost dog. When a stranger returns the dog, the contract that comes into existence is BEST classified as which of the following?

answers.text: a bilateral contract requiring an exchange of promises
a unilateral contract
an implied-in-law contract
an option contract requiring separate consideration

explanations.a: A reward offer does not require the finder to make a return promise, so it is not bilateral.
explanations.b: A reward offer is accepted by the act of performing the requested task, which is the classic unilateral contract structure.
explanations.c: An implied-in-law contract is a court-created remedy to prevent unjust enrichment, not a reward arrangement.
explanations.d: An option contract requires separate consideration to keep an offer open, which is not what a reward offer involves.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A contract entered into for an illegal purpose, such as the purchase of contraband, is which of the following from the moment of formation?

answers.text: voidable at the option of either party
enforceable only if both parties act in good faith
void as a matter of law
subject to later ratification by the parties

explanations.a: An illegal contract is not merely voidable; it has no legal force from the start.
explanations.b: Good faith cannot cure illegality; courts will not enforce an unlawful agreement under any conditions.
explanations.c: Lawful object is an essential element of validity, so a contract for an illegal purpose is void as a matter of law.
explanations.d: Parties cannot ratify what was illegal at inception; the unlawful purpose prevents formation altogether.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A seller mails a properly addressed and stamped acceptance of the buyer's offer using ordinary postal mail. Under the traditional mailbox rule, acceptance is generally effective:

answers.text: when the acceptance is dispatched into the mail
when the acceptance physically arrives at the buyer's address
only when the buyer personally reads the acceptance
only after the buyer acknowledges receipt in writing

explanations.a: Under the mailbox rule, acceptance by an authorized means is effective at the moment of dispatch, not on receipt.
explanations.b: Receipt is the rule for revocation, not for acceptance under the mailbox rule.
explanations.c: Personal reading is not required; dispatch alone is enough under the mailbox rule.
explanations.d: Written acknowledgment is also not required; the rule operates at dispatch.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A defendant in a breach-of-contract suit asserts that her signature was obtained while she was so intoxicated that she could not understand what she was signing. If proven, this defense generally renders the contract:

answers.text: fully enforceable as signed
automatically void with no further action
governed exclusively by the parol evidence rule
voidable at the defendant's option

explanations.a: Severe intoxication that prevents understanding undermines capacity, so the contract is not simply enforceable as signed.
explanations.b: The contract is not automatically void; the incapacitated party chooses whether to disaffirm once capacity is restored.
explanations.c: The parol evidence rule limits use of extrinsic evidence to vary written terms; it does not address incapacity.
explanations.d: Lack of contractual capacity due to severe intoxication makes the contract voidable at the affected party's option.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A purchase contract that fails to clearly identify the buyer and the seller may be:

answers.text: cured automatically by the closing attorney at settlement
enforceable so long as the price is stated
unenforceable for lack of an essential term
ratified by the broker on behalf of the parties

explanations.a: Closing attorneys cannot supply essential terms that the parties failed to agree on in the contract.
explanations.b: Price is necessary but not sufficient; the parties to the agreement must also be identifiable.
explanations.c: Identification of the parties is an essential term, and its absence renders the contract unenforceable.
explanations.d: A broker has no authority to ratify a contract on behalf of the buyer or the seller.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: Earnest money received by a real estate salesperson at the time an offer is signed must generally be:

answers.text: turned over promptly to the broker for placement in a designated trust account
cashed and stored in the salesperson's secure briefcase until closing
held by the salesperson personally until the buyer's loan funds
deposited into the listing brokerage's general operating account

explanations.a: License law requires earnest money to be promptly delivered to the broker for deposit into a designated trust or escrow account.
explanations.b: Holding cash personally creates serious risk of loss and violates trust-handling requirements.
explanations.c: Personal possession by the salesperson is not authorized; trust funds must be in a designated account.
explanations.d: Commingling earnest money with operating funds is a serious license law violation.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: To create a binding option contract, the option holder must generally provide which of the following to the property owner?

answers.text: a notarized copy of the proposed deed
written approval from the holder's lender
title insurance for the seller's benefit
separate consideration for the seller's promise to keep the offer open

explanations.a: A proposed deed is exchanged at closing if the option is exercised; it is not what makes the option binding.
explanations.b: Lender approval pertains to financing the eventual purchase, not to formation of the option itself.
explanations.c: Title insurance protects the buyer's title after closing; it has no role in creating the option.
explanations.d: An option is supported by separate consideration paid for the seller's promise to keep the offer open during the option period.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A purchase contract that is otherwise complete fails to specify a closing date. A court will MOST likely treat the contract as:

answers.text: automatically extended to a date one year after signing
calling for closing within a reasonable time
void unless the parties use a standard form
terminable only by mutual rescission of both parties

explanations.a: There is no automatic one-year extension; courts do not invent fixed deadlines that the parties did not agree on.
explanations.b: When a non-essential time term is missing, courts generally imply a reasonable time for performance.
explanations.c: Use of a standard form is not required for enforceability of an otherwise complete contract.
explanations.d: Missing terms do not automatically lock the contract until mutual rescission; courts can supply reasonable terms.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A purchase contract states that if the buyer fails to close, the seller may keep the buyer's earnest money as the seller's sole remedy. This provision is BEST described as a:

answers.text: penalty clause that courts will refuse to enforce
specific performance clause
rescission provision triggered by the buyer's request
liquidated damages clause

explanations.a: A penalty seeks to punish breach beyond actual damages; reasonable forfeiture of earnest money is generally not treated as a penalty.
explanations.b: Specific performance compels the breaching party to perform; it is not what is described here.
explanations.c: Rescission undoes a contract by mutual consent; it is unrelated to forfeiture of earnest money on default.
explanations.d: An agreed remedy that fixes damages in advance for a defined breach is a liquidated damages clause.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: Which of the following is the MOST common contingency included in residential purchase contracts?

answers.text: a contingency that the buyer's relatives approve the property
a financing contingency requiring the buyer to obtain a loan
a contingency that the seller find a new home before closing
a contingency for the broker to be elected to a professional board

explanations.a: Approval by relatives is not a standard residential contingency.
explanations.b: Most residential buyers depend on financing, so a loan contingency is the most common contingency in standard purchase contracts.
explanations.c: A seller's home-of-choice contingency does occur but is far less common than a buyer financing contingency.
explanations.d: A broker's professional involvement is not a contingency in a purchase contract between buyer and seller.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A purchase contract is contingent on the buyer's satisfactory home inspection. After the inspection reveals significant defects and the seller refuses to remedy them, the buyer typically may:

answers.text: terminate the contract under the contingency and recover the earnest money
only seek damages in court for the cost of repairs
be required to close at the original contract price
assign the contract to a different buyer without the seller's consent

explanations.a: When an inspection contingency is not satisfied and the seller will not address the issues, the buyer may terminate and recover earnest money under the contingency.
explanations.b: A buyer is not limited to a damages claim when the contingency itself provides a termination right.
explanations.c: The buyer is not forced to close when an unresolved inspection contingency permits termination.
explanations.d: Most purchase contracts restrict assignment without the seller's consent; the contingency does not authorize unilateral assignment.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.objective: 1C8 Duties and obligations of the parties
questions.text: A buyer is ready, willing, and able to close on the agreed date and tenders the funds at closing. The seller refuses to convey the property. The buyer's most powerful remedy is generally to:

answers.text: claim adverse possession of the property immediately
sue for specific performance to compel conveyance
file a mechanic's lien against the seller's other property
report the seller to the local zoning board

explanations.a: Adverse possession requires years of open, hostile, continuous use; it is not a remedy for a seller's breach of a sale contract.
explanations.b: Because each parcel of real estate is considered unique, courts will commonly grant a buyer specific performance to compel conveyance.
explanations.c: A mechanic's lien is for unpaid labor or materials supplied to a property, not for a seller's breach of contract.
explanations.d: Zoning boards regulate land use; they have no jurisdiction over a private sale dispute.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A listing agreement is BEST characterized as which of the following kinds of contracts, which generally cannot be assigned to another broker without the seller's consent?

answers.text: an option to purchase the property
a recordable instrument similar to a deed
a quasi-contract imposed by the courts
a personal services contract

explanations.a: An option to purchase gives the holder a unilateral right to buy in exchange for consideration; a listing is not a right held by the broker to acquire the property.
explanations.b: Listings are not recorded in the public land records like deeds; they are private agreements between the seller and the broker.
explanations.c: Quasi-contracts are court-imposed remedies for unjust enrichment, not voluntary listings.
explanations.d: A listing is a personal services contract for the broker's professional efforts and generally cannot be assigned without the seller's consent.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: To be enforceable, a written listing agreement should include all of the following EXCEPT:

answers.text: the buyer's preapproval letter from a lender
a definite expiration date for the listing
the brokerage's compensation
an adequate description or address of the property

explanations.a: A buyer's preapproval letter relates to a future purchase contract, not to the seller-broker listing agreement.
explanations.b: A definite end date is required so the parties know when their obligations end.
explanations.c: Compensation terms must be stated so the broker's pay obligation is clear.
explanations.d: The property must be identified clearly enough that the parties know what is being marketed.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: Under a typical exclusive listing agreement, the listing broker has a duty to:

answers.text: pay for all advertising costs out of personal funds
guarantee a sale at the listed price
use reasonable efforts to market the property and find a buyer
refuse to share information with cooperating brokers

explanations.a: Allocation of advertising costs is a matter of agreement; there is no general rule requiring the broker to bear them personally.
explanations.b: No broker can guarantee a sale at a particular price; markets and buyers control that outcome.
explanations.c: The broker's central undertaking is reasonable diligence in marketing the property and seeking a ready, willing, and able buyer.
explanations.d: Refusing to cooperate with other brokers usually disserves the seller and conflicts with the duty to market the property effectively.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A listing agreement is in effect when the seller unexpectedly dies. With respect to the listing, the seller's death generally:

answers.text: terminates the listing by operation of law
requires the broker to keep marketing the property for the heirs
extends the listing automatically until the estate is settled
converts the listing into a buyer-broker agreement

explanations.a: Death of the principal terminates the agency relationship by operation of law because the principal can no longer authorize the agent's acts.
explanations.b: The broker has no authority to keep marketing on behalf of a deceased principal; any new arrangement must be made with the personal representative of the estate.
explanations.c: There is no automatic extension; the agency simply ends.
explanations.d: Death of the seller does not transform a listing into an agreement to represent a buyer.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A seller signs separate listing agreements with three different brokers, agreeing to pay a commission only to the broker who actually procures a buyer. This arrangement is BEST classified as:

answers.text: a net listing among multiple brokers
an open listing
an exclusive-agency listing with multiple firms
a multiple-listing service entry

explanations.a: A net listing pays the broker any amount over a specified net to the seller; the description here does not match.
explanations.b: An open listing allows the seller to engage multiple brokers and pay only the one who procures a buyer.
explanations.c: Exclusive agency gives one broker exclusive rights among brokers, not multiple firms competing on equal footing.
explanations.d: A multiple-listing service is a cooperative database, not a type of listing contract by itself.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.objective: 1E Employment agreements between broker and licensees
questions.text: Under the typical relationship between a broker and an affiliated licensee, the broker is generally responsible for which of the following?

answers.text: paying the licensee's federal income tax withholding
providing the licensee with health and dental insurance
scheduling the licensee's open-house attendance hour by hour
supervising the licensed activities of the licensee on behalf of clients

explanations.a: Income tax withholding generally does not apply to independent-contractor licensees; the licensee handles her own self-employment tax.
explanations.b: Standard employee benefits such as health and dental coverage are not required for independent-contractor licensees.
explanations.c: Hour-by-hour scheduling is characteristic of employment, not the typical broker-licensee independent-contractor model.
explanations.d: Regardless of tax classification, license law makes the broker responsible for supervising the licensed real estate activities of affiliated licensees.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A real estate sale has closed and the deed has been delivered to and accepted by the buyer. With respect to the contract status, the transaction is BEST described as:

answers.text: a bilateral executory agreement still requiring further performance
an executed transaction reflecting fully completed performance
a voidable conveyance pending the seller's post-closing approval
an executory agreement because future mortgage payments remain

explanations.a: The transaction is no longer bilateral and pending; both parties have performed.
explanations.b: Once the deed has been delivered and accepted and all obligations met, the transaction is executed.
explanations.c: A properly closed and delivered deed is not subject to the seller's second-guessing after the fact.
explanations.d: The buyer's remaining mortgage obligations run to the lender, not to the seller under the purchase contract; the sale itself is complete.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.keyword: exclusive agency no commission on owner sale
questions.text: Under an exclusive-agency listing, the seller finds and contracts directly with a buyer entirely through her own efforts, with no involvement by the listing broker. In this situation, the listing broker is:

answers.text: entitled to the full commission because any exclusive listing protects the broker
not entitled to a commission because the seller procured the buyer herself
entitled to half the normal commission as a flat marketing fee
required to file a claim in court to determine whether any commission is owed

explanations.a: Unlike an exclusive-right-to-sell, an exclusive-agency listing preserves the seller's right to sell directly without owing a commission.
explanations.b: Exclusive agency protects the broker only against competing brokers; a seller retains the right to sell personally without triggering a commission.
explanations.c: No partial commission is automatically owed when the seller independently procures the buyer under an exclusive-agency listing.
explanations.d: The listing contract terms are clear; no litigation is needed to determine that no commission is owed when the seller sells herself.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A buyer's agent fails to check publicly available flood zone maps before advising the buyer that the property carries no flood risk, when in fact it lies within a designated flood zone. The agent may be in breach of which duty?

answers.text: exercising the competence that a reasonably skilled agent would provide
maintaining client information as strictly confidential
accounting for all funds received from the client
following all lawful instructions from the principal

explanations.a: The duty of skill and care requires an agent to exercise the competence of a reasonably skilled practitioner, which includes researching publicly available information before advising a client.
explanations.b: Confidentiality concerns protecting the client's information, not the agent's competence in research.
explanations.c: Accounting concerns the proper handling of money and property, which is not at issue in this scenario.
explanations.d: The duty of obedience concerns following lawful instructions; the agent's failure here is one of research, not disobedience.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: Both buyer and seller sign a purchase contract for a parcel they both believe is five acres, when it is actually two acres. A court may allow either party to:

answers.text: immediately record a deed for the full five acres
rescind the contract on grounds of mutual mistake of fact
enforce the contract as written and pursue damages only
demand a third-party appraisal to determine the correct price

explanations.a: Neither party can create a right to five acres simply by recording a deed when only two acres exist.
explanations.b: When both parties are mistaken about a material fact that was the basis of the bargain, equity may permit rescission.
explanations.c: Mutual mistake can be grounds for rescission, not just damages; enforcing as written is not the only option.
explanations.d: An appraisal addresses value, not the factual error about acreage that gave rise to the mistake.

questions.name: Agency Relationships and Contracts
questions.text: A buyer submits a written offer stating that it must be accepted within 72 hours. The seller does not respond within that period. The offer has:

answers.text: lapsed and is no longer available for acceptance
remained in force because the seller has not formally rejected it
automatically converted into a right of first refusal
been extended by operation of law until the seller provides a response

explanations.a: An offer that specifies a deadline for acceptance lapses automatically when that deadline passes without a response.
explanations.b: The absence of a formal rejection does not keep the offer alive past its stated deadline.
explanations.c: Lapse of an offer has no legal mechanism that converts it into a right of first refusal.
explanations.d: There is no legal rule that extends an offer beyond its stated deadline; it expires by its own terms.
